definition: OpenCog is a project that aims to build an open source artificial intelligence framework.
details: OpenCog Prime is an architecture for robot and virtual embodied cognition that defines a set of interacting components designed to give rise to human-equivalent artificial general intelligence (AGI) as an emergent phenomenon of the whole system. OpenCog Prime's design is primarily the work of Ben Goertzel while the OpenCog framework is intended as a generic framework for broad-based AGI research. Research utilizing OpenCog has been published in journals and presented at conferences and workshops including the annual Conference on Artificial General Intelligence. OpenCog is released under the terms of the GNU Affero General Public License. OpenCog is in use by more than 50 companies, including Huawei and Cisco.

explainer.lead: OpenCog is a project aiming to build an open-source artificial intelligence framework, with OpenCog Prime as an architecture for robot and virtual embodied cognition. It matters as a long-running attempt to reach human-equivalent AGI as an emergent property of interacting components.

tiers.eli5: It is a big open toolbox whose parts are meant to work together so that, as a whole, they act as intelligent as a person.
tiers.practitioner: Researchers build on the framework for broad-based AGI research, with work published in journals and at conferences and workshops. The pitfall is that the design targets emergence of general intelligence from many components, which is hard to verify.
tiers.paperLevel: OpenCog Prime defines interacting components intended to give rise to human-equivalent artificial general intelligence as an emergent phenomenon of the whole system; the framework is generic for AGI research. Its design is primarily the work of Ben Goertzel.

explainer.example: A research group can use the OpenCog framework as the base for an AGI experiment, with OpenCog Prime supplying the component architecture.
